changes: Shared and private project documents with explicit CLI discovery and checks.
applies_when: A project wants document entry points.
steps: Run docs setup; retain existing files, use relative shared links and ignored private notes; run docs check.
no_change_when: Existing projects without document registration keep working.

changes: Ordinary commands execute the latest compatible stable release; project version tasks and policies removed.
configuration: Legacy echo-kit.py and echo-kit.lock.json; --task and updates apply removed.
applies_when: A project uses a generated version-pinned entry or task workflow.
steps: Read updates setup help; finish active business operations/cleanup, then migrate generated entries with backups. Preserve custom entries and historical evidence; call echo-kit directly.
no_change_when: Direct CLI users need no project version files or tasks.

changes: Dependency-aware parallel service startup, bounded by a default of four in this release.
configuration: [service_startup] concurrency and services up/restart --jobs; existing depends and prepare.
applies_when: Service startup previously relied on implicit serial order.
steps: Declare real dependencies; keep shared builds in project scripts and use --jobs 1 for diagnostics. Inspect partial failures without automatic rollback.
no_change_when: Existing explicit dependencies and project adapters remain valid.

changes: Managed Docker browsers are headed with read-only noVNC; default service concurrency covers all selected services.
configuration: browser.headless, viewer_port, auto_open; explicit concurrency limits remain; external browser.endpoint stays external.
applies_when: An old container/config lacks viewing or a project expects the old implicit concurrency limit.
steps: Read browser status and active operations. After operations finish, explicitly browser down/up to recreate an owned container. For external endpoints, inspect configuration source and adjust only within authorization; never stop or adopt the external container. Set concurrency explicitly if needed.
no_change_when: Current managed containers can be reused; explicit headless/external choices and explicit concurrency limits are preserved. An upgrade alone never migrates external browsers.

changes: guide combines current Skill, protocol and release notes; updates notes explains adaptation; browser results disclose capabilities. Docker is the recommended frontend debugging route.
configuration: No new project settings. Existing browser.endpoint is an explicit compatibility exception.
applies_when: AI uses copied Kit instructions or assumes an upgraded tool migrated its project/browser.
steps: Read guide for the relevant Skill on first session use and after execution-version changes. Use updates notes --since VERSION only when that earlier version is known. Keep project facts/team rules and replace copied generic instructions with a short CLI pointer. Inspect external capability reports before proposing authorized migration.
no_change_when: Existing documents, exports, adapters and external instances are preserved. No acknowledgement files, version locks or mandatory migration.

changes: Windows desktop tray discovers registered owned services and browser containers. Reopen an existing debugging viewer without messaging AI or restarting an experiment.
configuration: Automatic tray is off for CI, noninteractive sessions and ECHO_KIT_TRAY=0. No browser port or project configuration changes.
applies_when: Windows users want to recover a closed noVNC tab while resources are running.
steps: Start services or browser normally, or run tray start in an existing workspace. Choose the project viewer from the tray menu. tray status/stop require no workspace; stopping the tray leaves business resources intact.
no_change_when: Other platforms keep CLI/viewer links. Headless and legacy browsers have no viewer. External instances are excluded. No service daemon or boot startup is installed.

changes: Windows tray uses the same environment windowless Python launcher, preventing a persistent console from virtual-environment redirector children.
configuration: No project setting changes. The Windows Python environment must include pythonw.exe.
applies_when: A 0.8.0 tray displays a blank terminal window.
steps: After upgrading, run tray stop then tray start in a registered project to replace the existing UI process. This does not stop services, containers or experiments.
no_change_when: Existing business resources and browser state remain unchanged. A running older tray is not automatically replaced.

changes: Remove the redundant Refresh tray menu item. Resource state still updates automatically every five seconds.
steps: After upgrading, restart only the tray to see the simplified menu; no manual refresh is needed.
no_change_when: Business services, browser pages and experiments are unaffected.

changes: Onboarding checks test identity prerequisites and guides explicit project-owned preparation, verification and cleanup. Skill reads include the bundled identity reference.
configuration: No new commands, project settings or account storage.
applies_when: Requested cases require authenticated identities, roles or tenant membership.
steps: Read guide echo-init; reuse project account preparation or add a project script when absent. Execute within existing authorization, verify login and required role/tenant, and retain only appropriate reusable identities.
no_change_when: Anonymous cases skip preparation. Existing scripts, auth adapters, business accounts and exported project edits remain unchanged.

changes: Guidance separates shared team configuration, machine-local overrides, runtime registration and secrets.
configuration: Existing echo-kit.toml, .echo-kit/local.toml and environment tables; merge behavior unchanged.
applies_when: Onboarding or debugging requires local ports, paths or other machine-specific settings.
steps: Read guide echo-init; classify values, use minimal local overrides in the matching environment, reconcile startup and readiness, verify ignore and tracking status. Compare exported copies in an empty directory before merging.
no_change_when: Correctly separated existing projects need no migration. No automatic port allocation or business project changes.

changes: Case categories/search and layered guides; runs list defaults to paginated summaries instead of complete records.
configuration: Optional cases description/category/tags/docs. Existing execution and configuration precedence unchanged.
applies_when: Discovering growing experiment collections, reading guides or consuming runs list JSON.
steps: Use cases list/show; read guide topics before the relevant capability, --full for full references. Update runs list consumers from an array to items plus pagination; use runs show for full records. skills show no longer auto-appends references. Preserve existing project files and exported edits.
no_change_when: Existing lab/verify adapters and unannotated cases keep running. No automatic script moves, private reads or history deletion.

changes: Managed resource_id now identifies one shared local service instance across workspaces. Cases use shared service leases by default; browsers stay workspace-local. Tray groups shared instances separately.
configuration: Optional cases.NAME.service_access=shared|exclusive. Explicit service IDs require compatible launch inputs. Machine-specific mappings and browser ports belong in local.toml.
applies_when: Multiple workspaces use one managed microservice, or existing exclusive-by-default cases modify shared data.
steps: Read guide echo-workbench --topic services. Set exclusive access for cases that cannot safely share data. Finish old operations before adopting legacy registrations via services up in the original workspace. Use named down/restart for borrowed services; unnamed commands affect only instances started here. Replace an older tray with tray stop/start. Use the new version in every cooperating session.
no_change_when: No-ID services retain workspace/environment-local identity. External instances, business configurations, historical evidence and exported Skills are not automatically migrated. No release or business operations are implied.

changes: Workspace-wide Markdown map, directory AGENTS.md context, bounded explicit document reads and structural rule checks.
configuration: No new configuration or document registry. Existing shared/private ownership and workspace boundaries still apply.
applies_when: Finding module documentation, choosing where rules belong or inspecting nested AGENTS.md outside echo/.
steps: Read the documents guide topic. Use docs map/context/read before editing; put global constraints at root and local constraints in the relevant directory, linking detailed requirements. Run docs check --rules; retain ordinary docs check for registered shared/private entries. Treat partial/unsupported discovery as unverified, not a complete client instruction view.
no_change_when: Existing documents, exported Skills and business repositories are not moved or overwritten. Semantic conflict resolution remains the agent and user responsibility. Runtime commands are not blocked by document checks.

changes: Concurrent update checks wait up to three seconds and reuse completed checks. Online commands can fall back to verified cached newer runtimes; subcommand help follows routing.
configuration: No project changes. Interpreter-specific prepared version metadata is stored in user update cache.
applies_when: Parallel commands use an older installed entry, or release discovery/preparation is temporarily unavailable.
steps: Upgrade the installed entry once from official PyPI to receive this router fix. Verify the PATH entry version; use updates check for diagnosis and ordinary subcommand help for routed help. Do not retry a business operation on another version after it started.
no_change_when: Explicit offline calls stay on the calling package. Top-level help/version and runtime info remain local diagnostics. Business projects and exported Skills are not automatically modified.

changes: Root includes explicitly load module TOML configurations for projects, services, auth and cases; workspace check and cases show expose value-free configuration provenance.
configuration: Optional root includes array. Module definitions share one workspace; existing local and environment precedence is unchanged.
applies_when: A growing workspace needs separate module-owned configuration files.
steps: Read the configuration topic; keep small projects in one file. Move each definition once, preserve IDs and existing relative-path meanings, list files explicitly, and inspect workspace check / cases show sources. Track shared modules in Git; keep machine-specific changes in local.toml.
no_change_when: Existing single-file projects require no migration. No directory scans, private includes, automatic business edits or exported-Skill overwrites.

changes: Manual resolution can close abandoned operations with no held resources. Legacy service adoption recognizes explicitly resolved runs while retaining their original evidence. Update checks use unique batch identities instead of clock equality, so sequential checks on coarse Windows clocks still refresh.
applies_when: An exited operation has no held resources but remains unfinished, or preserved active evidence blocks adoption after manual resolution.
steps: Verify business work and cleanup are finished before operations resolve ID --note. Retry legacy service adoption only after resolution; matching workspace, environment, run and evidence identity are required. Live processes still block resolution. 0.12.1 publication was blocked by CI and was not released.
no_change_when: Active operations, unresolved cleanup and unconfirmed process ownership remain protected. No automatic resolution, evidence deletion or service restart.

changes: --version follows ordinary update routing and prints the executing version. Successful transfer notices hide source-entry versions and are silent for version queries. runtime info adds version_scope=installed_entry.
configuration: No workspace configuration changes; explicit offline version queries stay local.
applies_when: Version output from an older installed entry is mistaken for the version used by ordinary commands.
steps: Upgrade the installed entry once to acquire the new --version behavior; verify its PATH and --offline --version. Use --version for daily queries, runtime info for entry diagnosis, and run records for operation provenance.
no_change_when: No global self-replacement or project migration. Existing update checks, cached runtime validation and no-retry-after-business rules remain intact.

changes: AI may explicitly release confirmed stale operation reservations without a separate user confirmation. Help and notes distinguish reservation release from business cleanup.
configuration: No configuration or command changes. Existing process checks and manually_resolved records remain compatible.
applies_when: An exited operation leaves a stale reservation, including failed browser preparation or experiments without cleanup adapters.
steps: Inspect operations show and evidence, confirm execution processes and children have exited, then resolve with a note recording checks and reason. Use cleanup adapters when needed; retain outstanding cleanup facts. Re-export old project guides to an empty directory and compare/merge.
no_change_when: Active execution processes and children still block resolution. No automatic release, service stop, data deletion or evidence rewrite. Known remote tasks require separate state verification; ask for genuinely uncertain state or actions beyond authorization.

changes: Acceptance guidance distinguishes human testing, one-off AI interaction and repeatable experiments; scripts and cases are no longer the default prerequisite.
configuration: No new commands or configuration fields.
applies_when: Simple acceptance was spending time creating permanent browser scripts and case definitions.
steps: Choose the approach from user intent. Human testing uses the business URL; AI interaction needs a compatible live browser session and resource protection. Reuse or create cases only when repeatability is useful. Read the browser topic for the temporary-session reference.
no_change_when: Existing cases remain valid. Authorization, cleanup and evidence requirements remain. noVNC stays read-only; old project exports require comparison and merge.
